title: Moving the goalposts
settingKo: 고객이 계속 요구를 바꾸는 상황을 동료와 관용구를 섞어 이야기합니다.

lines.text: Every time we hit the target, they move the goalposts, and now they want the whole thing in three languages by Monday.
lines.ko: 목표를 맞출 때마다 골대를 옮기더니 이젠 월요일까지 3개 언어로 다 해 달래요.

lines.text: We need to nip this in the bud, or we'll be doing free work for them until the end of time.
lines.ko: 싹부터 잘라야 해요, 안 그러면 영원히 공짜로 일해 주게 될 거예요.

lines.text: Agreed, but they're our biggest account, so we can't exactly put our foot down without a plan B.
lines.ko: 동의해요. 그래도 최대 고객이라 대안 없이 강하게 나갈 순 없어요.

lines.text: Then let's put a change-request process in writing, so every extra ask comes with a price tag.
lines.ko: 그럼 변경 요청 절차를 문서로 만들어서 추가 요구마다 가격표가 붙게 하죠.

phrases.en: They keep moving the goalposts.
We need to nip this in the bud.

response.situationKo: 상사가 프로젝트 중간에 또 범위를 늘립니다. 관용구를 섞어 선을 그어 보세요.
response.prompt: Oh, and could we squeeze in a mobile version as well? Same deadline.

answers.text: I'd love to, but something has to give. Either the deadline moves or the scope shrinks.
answers.noteKo: something has to give는 '뭔가는 포기해야 해요'예요.

answers.text: Realistically, that would stretch us too thin. Which part matters most to you?
We can absolutely do it, just not by Friday without cutting corners. That's the trade-off.
Ha, the classic scope creep! Let's talk about what we can drop to make room.
answers.noteKo: scope creep는 범위가 슬금슬금 늘어나는 현상이에요.

title: Saying no without saying no
settingKo: 임원 회의에서 상대의 제안에 직접 반대하지 않고 우려를 전합니다.

lines.text: I'm inclined to think we should launch in all twelve markets at once and capture the momentum.
lines.ko: 12개 시장에 한꺼번에 출시해서 기세를 타야 한다고 봅니다.

lines.text: I can certainly see the appeal, and I'd hate to dampen the enthusiasm in the room.
lines.ko: 그 매력은 충분히 이해되고, 회의실의 열기에 찬물을 끼얹고 싶진 않아요.

lines.text: That said, I do wonder whether our support team could realistically absorb twelve launches in the same month.
lines.ko: 그렇긴 하지만 지원팀이 같은 달에 출시 12건을 현실적으로 감당할 수 있을지는 의문이에요.

lines.text: Fair point. Perhaps a staggered rollout over a quarter would give us the best of both worlds.
lines.ko: 일리 있어요. 분기에 걸쳐 단계적으로 출시하면 두 마리 토끼를 다 잡을 수 있겠네요.

phrases.en: I can certainly see the appeal.
That said, I do wonder whether...

response.situationKo: 동료의 아이디어가 위험해 보입니다. 직접 반대하지 말고 완곡하게 우려를 표현해 보세요.
response.prompt: So, everyone on board with dropping the free plan entirely?

answers.text: I can see the logic. That said, I wonder how many of our paying users started on the free plan.
It might be worth testing it in one market before we commit across the board.
I'd be curious to see the churn numbers first. Gut feeling says it could backfire.
Mostly on board, but I've got a nagging feeling we're underestimating the free users.

title: Oh, brilliant
settingKo: 친구의 반어적인 말투를 알아듣고 맞받아칩니다.

lines.text: Oh, brilliant. The train's cancelled, it's pouring, and I left my umbrella at the office. Best day ever.
lines.ko: 아주 훌륭하네. 기차는 취소, 비는 쏟아지고, 우산은 회사에 두고 왔어. 최고의 하루야.

lines.text: Living the dream, then. Want me to come and pick you up, or are you enjoying the drama too much?
lines.ko: 꿈같은 삶이네. 데리러 갈까, 아니면 이 드라마를 너무 즐기는 중이야?

lines.text: Ha. If you could rescue me before I dissolve completely, that would be lovely.
lines.ko: 하. 내가 완전히 녹아내리기 전에 구해 주면 정말 고맙겠어.

lines.text: On my way. Try not to make any more life choices in the next fifteen minutes.
lines.ko: 가는 중. 앞으로 15분 동안은 인생의 결정을 더 내리지 말고 있어.

gist.questionKo: 첫 번째 사람의 '최고의 하루'는 무슨 뜻인가요?

phrases.en: Living the dream.
That would be lovely.

response.situationKo: 친구가 반어적으로 투덜댑니다. 같은 톤으로 받아쳐 보세요.
response.prompt: Great, another meeting that could have been an email. My favorite.

answers.text: Oh, the highlight of the week. I can't wait to hear the same update for the fourth time.
Thrilling. Shall I bring snacks to stay awake?
Same. Maybe we can suggest an agenda and finish in ten minutes.
I share your enthusiasm entirely. Let's at least sit near the door.

title: Countering the offer
settingKo: 이직 제안을 받은 후 연봉과 조건을 정교하게 협상합니다.

lines.text: We're excited about you joining, and the offer reflects the top of our band for this level.
lines.ko: 합류해 주셔서 기쁘고, 이 제안은 이 직급 연봉 범위의 최상단이에요.

lines.text: I appreciate that, and I'm genuinely keen. I'm just weighing it against a competing offer that's around ten percent higher.
lines.ko: 감사하고 정말 가고 싶어요. 다만 10퍼센트쯤 높은 다른 제안과 비교하고 있어요.

lines.text: Base is fairly fixed, but there may be some flexibility on the signing bonus and equity.
lines.ko: 기본급은 거의 고정이지만 입사 보너스와 지분은 유연성이 있을 수 있어요.

lines.text: That could bridge the gap. If we can get the first-year total to match, I'd be happy to sign this week.
lines.ko: 그럼 차이를 메울 수 있겠네요. 첫해 총액만 맞춰 주시면 이번 주에 서명할게요.

phrases.en: There may be some flexibility.
That could bridge the gap.

response.situationKo: 회사가 연봉은 못 올린다고 합니다. 다른 조건으로 가치를 끌어내 보세요.
response.prompt: I'm afraid the salary really can't move any higher.

answers.text: Understood. In that case, would you consider a salary review after six months instead of twelve?
Fair enough. Could we look at an extra week of leave or two remote days a week?
I respect that. Would a more senior title be possible, given the scope of the role?
OK, no worries. Then let's get creative with the benefits side.
answers.noteKo: get creative는 다른 방식을 찾자는 뜻이에요.

title: A hostile interview
settingKo: 방송 인터뷰에서 진행자의 공격적인 질문을 침착하게 받아냅니다.

lines.text: With respect, your company raised prices twice this year while reporting record profits. Isn't that simply greed?
lines.ko: 실례지만 귀사는 기록적 이익을 내면서 올해 가격을 두 번 올렸어요. 그건 그냥 탐욕 아닌가요?

lines.text: I understand why it looks that way, and I won't pretend the timing was ideal.
lines.ko: 그렇게 보이는 이유는 이해하고, 시기가 이상적이었다고 둘러대지 않겠습니다.

lines.text: But most of that profit came from one division, and the price rises were in another, where costs went up by a third.
lines.ko: 다만 이익 대부분은 한 사업부에서 났고, 가격 인상은 비용이 3분의 1 오른 다른 사업부였습니다.

lines.text: So you're saying customers should simply accept it?
lines.ko: 그러니까 고객이 그냥 받아들여야 한다는 겁니까?

options: 이익과 가격 인상은 다른 사업부의 일이다

phrases.en: I understand why it looks that way.
I won't pretend the timing was ideal.

response.situationKo: 기자가 말을 왜곡해서 되묻습니다. 침착하게 바로잡아 보세요.
response.prompt: So you're saying customers should simply accept it?

answers.text: That's not what I said. What I'm saying is that we owe customers a clear explanation, which is why I'm here.
answers.noteKo: That's not what I said로 왜곡을 바로잡아요.

answers.text: To be clear, no. We're freezing prices for the next twelve months, starting today.
Let me be clear: customers deserve better, and here's specifically what we're doing about it.
Not at all, and I'd push back on that framing a little.
answers.noteKo: push back on that framing은 그 프레임에 반박하다예요.

title: Where do you draw the line?
settingKo: 저녁 자리에서 SNS 규제와 표현의 자유를 깊이 있게 토론합니다.

lines.text: I'm all for free speech, but platforms that profit from outrage can't claim to be neutral bystanders.
lines.ko: 표현의 자유는 찬성이지만 분노로 돈 버는 플랫폼이 중립적 방관자라고 할 순 없어.

lines.text: Sure, but the moment governments decide what's acceptable, you've handed them a tool they'll eventually misuse.
lines.ko: 그렇지, 근데 정부가 뭐가 괜찮은지 정하는 순간 결국 악용할 도구를 넘겨주는 거야.

lines.text: So where would you draw the line, if not at the algorithm that decides what goes viral?
lines.ko: 그럼 무엇을 퍼뜨릴지 정하는 알고리즘이 아니면 어디에 선을 긋겠어?

lines.text: Maybe that's exactly it: regulate the amplification, not the speech itself.
lines.ko: 바로 그거일지도 몰라. 말 자체가 아니라 증폭을 규제하는 거지.

phrases.en: I'm all for free speech, but...
Where would you draw the line?

response.situationKo: 민감한 사회 이슈에 대해 양쪽을 인정하면서 자기 입장을 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: Should schools ban phones completely?

answers.text: On balance, I'd lean towards a ban during lessons, while allowing them at lunch.
I'm torn. The strongest argument for a ban is focus, but the strongest against is safety on the way home.
While I see the benefits, a total ban feels like treating the symptom rather than the cause.
Honestly? Yes. Kids barely talk to each other at break anymore.

title: Steering away from politics
settingKo: 가족 저녁 식사에서 정치 논쟁이 격해지자 화제를 부드럽게 돌립니다.

lines.text: Honestly, anyone who voted for that lot needs their head examined.
lines.ko: 솔직히 그 사람들한테 투표한 사람은 머리 검사 좀 받아 봐야 해.

lines.text: Well, I suspect we're not going to settle the election over Mum's roast, are we?
lines.ko: 음, 엄마가 만든 로스트 앞에서 선거 결판낼 건 아니잖아, 그렇지?

lines.text: Speaking of which, has anyone actually tried the new bakery on the high street? I've heard mixed reviews.
lines.ko: 말 나온 김에, 대로변에 새로 생긴 빵집 가 본 사람 있어? 평이 엇갈리던데.

lines.text: Ha, nice try. But fine, the croissants are overpriced and the coffee's excellent.
lines.ko: 하, 잘 돌렸네. 좋아, 크루아상은 비싸고 커피는 훌륭해.

phrases.en: We're not going to settle it over dinner.
Speaking of which...

response.situationKo: 모임에서 누군가 민감한 주제로 언성을 높입니다. 분위기를 해치지 않고 화제를 돌려 보세요.
response.prompt: And another thing about religion that really gets me...

answers.text: Let's maybe save that one for another night. On a lighter note, how was everyone's holiday?
answers.noteKo: On a lighter note는 가벼운 화제로 넘어갈 때 써요.

answers.text: I can tell this one's close to your heart. Speaking of hearts, how's your sister's wedding planning going?
Changing the subject entirely, has anyone seen that documentary everyone's talking about?
answers.noteKo: Changing the subject entirely로 솔직하게 전환해요.

answers.text: Okay, okay, truce! Who wants more wine?

title: Thirty seconds with an investor
settingKo: 행사장에서 유명 투자자를 만나 30초 안에 회사를 소개합니다.

lines.text: I've got about a minute before my next panel. What are you working on?
lines.ko: 다음 패널까지 1분쯤 있어요. 뭘 하고 계세요?

lines.text: Small clinics lose roughly a fifth of their revenue to missed appointments, and we've cut that in half for our first forty clients.
lines.ko: 소규모 병원은 노쇼로 매출의 약 5분의 1을 잃는데, 저희는 첫 고객 40곳에서 그걸 절반으로 줄였어요.

lines.text: Interesting. How, exactly, and what's stopping a big player from copying you?
lines.ko: 흥미롭네요. 정확히 어떻게요? 그리고 대기업이 따라 하지 못하게 하는 건 뭐죠?

lines.text: We predict who's likely to miss and fill those slots automatically. The moat is three years of scheduling data no one else has.
lines.ko: 노쇼 가능성을 예측해서 그 자리를 자동으로 채워요. 해자는 아무도 없는 3년 치 예약 데이터예요.

phrases.en: What's stopping a big player from copying you?
phrases.ko: 대기업이 따라 하지 못하게 하는 건 뭐죠?

phrases.en: The moat is our data.

response.situationKo: 누군가 당신의 일이나 프로젝트를 30초 안에 설명해 달라고 합니다.
response.prompt: In one breath, what do you do?

answers.text: We help small restaurants cut food waste so that they save around ten percent on ingredients.
answers.noteKo: We help A do B so that C 구조예요.

answers.text: In short, the problem is that freelancers get paid late, and we've built a way to get them paid on day one.
I translate legal contracts for startups, without the lawyer-sized bill.
I lead a team that makes hospital software easier for nurses, which, believe me, is long overdue.
answers.noteKo: long overdue는 진작 했어야 할 일이에요.

title: Being left on read
settingKo: 친구에게 연락이 끊긴 상대에 대해 하소연하고 친구가 현실적으로 조언합니다.

lines.text: Three dates, great chemistry, and now he's left me on read for five days. I'm genuinely baffled.
lines.ko: 세 번 만나고 케미도 좋았는데 이제 5일째 읽씹이야. 진짜 어리둥절해.

lines.text: Oof. I hate to say it, but radio silence after date three usually speaks for itself.
lines.ko: 아이고. 이런 말 하기 싫지만 세 번째 데이트 후 무소식이면 보통 그게 답이야.

lines.text: Part of me wants to send one breezy message, just to have closure.
lines.ko: 마음 한편으론 정리라도 하게 가볍게 메시지 하나 보내고 싶어.

lines.text: Go for it, as long as you're genuinely fine with whatever comes back, including nothing at all.
lines.ko: 해 봐. 무슨 답이 오든, 아무 답이 없어도 정말 괜찮다면.

phrases.en: He left me on read.
It usually speaks for itself.

response.situationKo: 친구가 연애 고민을 털어놓습니다. 솔직하지만 다정하게 조언해 보세요.
response.prompt: Am I overthinking this, or is something off?

answers.text: Honestly, a bit of both. Trust your gut, but don't write the whole story before you have the facts.
answers.noteKo: Trust your gut은 직감을 믿으라는 말이에요.

answers.text: For what it's worth, you deserve someone who doesn't make you guess.
answers.noteKo: For what it's worth는 '내 생각엔'이라는 겸손한 표현이에요.

answers.text: It sounds like you already know the answer and just want permission to feel it.
You're spiraling a little, love. Put the phone down and let's get dinner.

title: A toast with a twist
settingKo: 형제의 결혼식에서 재치 있는 축사를 합니다.

lines.text: For those who don't know me, I'm Tom's older brother, which means I've had thirty years to collect material.
lines.ko: 저를 모르시는 분들을 위해, 톰의 형입니다. 즉 30년간 소재를 모아 왔다는 뜻이죠.

lines.text: Don't worry, Sarah, I've been told to keep it clean, so this will be a very short speech.
lines.ko: 걱정 마세요, 사라. 깨끗하게 하라고 해서 아주 짧은 축사가 될 거예요.

lines.text: Get on with it! We know all the stories anyway!
lines.ko: 빨리 해! 어차피 다 아는 얘기잖아!

lines.text: In all seriousness, I've never seen my brother as calm or as happy as he is with you. To Tom and Sarah!
lines.ko: 농담은 그만하고, 동생이 당신과 있을 때만큼 차분하고 행복한 걸 본 적이 없어요. 톰과 사라를 위하여!

options: 동생이 신부와 있을 때 가장 행복하다

phrases.en: I've had thirty years to collect material.
In all seriousness...

response.situationKo: 친구 생일 파티에서 짧고 재치 있는 축하 한마디를 해 보세요.
response.prompt: Speech! Speech!

answers.text: I'll keep this short, mainly because the cake is melting. Happy birthday, Jen. Here's to another year of terrible puns!
For those who don't know, Jen once drove four hours to bring me soup. In all seriousness, everyone should have a friend like her. Cheers!
I've known Jen for fifteen years, and she still hasn't learned how to whisper. Happy birthday!
Thank you all for coming. Jen, you make every room warmer. Here's to you.

title: Three a.m. outage
settingKo: 새벽에 서비스 장애가 나서 엔지니어 리더와 긴급 통화를 합니다.

lines.text: Payments have been failing for twenty minutes across Europe, and the error rate is still climbing.
lines.ko: 유럽 전역에서 20분째 결제가 실패하고 있고 오류율이 계속 오르고 있어요.

lines.text: Roll back last night's deploy first and ask questions later. We can diagnose once the bleeding stops.
lines.ko: 어젯밤 배포부터 롤백하고 질문은 나중에 해요. 출혈이 멈추면 진단할 수 있어요.

lines.text: Rolling back now. Should I post on the status page, or wait until we know the cause?
lines.ko: 지금 롤백 중이에요. 상태 페이지에 공지할까요, 원인을 알 때까지 기다릴까요?

lines.text: Post now. A vague update beats silence, and we'll follow up every thirty minutes until it's resolved.
lines.ko: 지금 올려요. 모호한 공지라도 침묵보다 낫고, 해결될 때까지 30분마다 업데이트할 거예요.

phrases.en: Once the bleeding stops.
A vague update beats silence.

response.situationKo: 장애 후 고객에게 상황을 설명하는 짧은 메시지를 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: Customers are asking what happened. What do we tell them?

answers.text: Between two and three a.m., some payments failed. We've identified the cause, and no data was lost.
answers.noteKo: 시간, 원인, 피해 범위를 간결하게 말해요.

answers.text: We sincerely apologize. The root cause was a faulty update, and we're putting in place extra checks to prevent a repeat.
Short version: we broke something, we fixed it, and we're making sure it can't happen the same way again.
Service is fully restored. A detailed report will follow within forty-eight hours.

title: The CFO isn't convinced
settingKo: 재무 담당 임원이 마케팅 예산을 깎으려 하자 데이터로 맞섭니다.

lines.text: Marketing spend is up forty percent year on year, and frankly, I struggle to see what we're getting for it.
lines.ko: 마케팅 비용이 전년 대비 40퍼센트 늘었는데 솔직히 뭘 얻고 있는지 모르겠어요.

lines.text: That's a reasonable challenge. The headline number hides the fact that cost per new customer actually fell by a quarter.
lines.ko: 합리적인 지적이에요. 총액만 보면 신규 고객당 비용이 사실 4분의 1 줄었다는 게 가려져요.

lines.text: Then why does it feel like revenue isn't keeping pace?
lines.ko: 그럼 왜 매출이 따라오지 못하는 느낌이죠?

lines.text: Because those customers are on annual plans, so most of their revenue lands next year, not this one.
lines.ko: 그 고객들이 연간 요금제라서 매출 대부분이 올해가 아니라 내년에 잡히기 때문이에요.

phrases.en: That's a reasonable challenge.
The headline number hides the fact that...

response.situationKo: 임원이 당신 팀의 성과를 의심합니다. 숫자와 맥락으로 방어해 보세요.
response.prompt: Convince me your team is worth the headcount.

answers.text: For every dollar we cost, we've saved roughly four in support costs since last spring.
answers.noteKo: For every로 투자 대비 효과를 말해요.

answers.text: The numbers show churn dropped from eight percent to five. Put another way, that's two hundred customers we kept.
answers.noteKo: Put another way로 체감되게 바꿔 말해요.

answers.text: With some context: we took on three projects nobody else wanted, and two are now profitable.
Fair ask. Give me ten minutes and one slide, and I think you'll be pleasantly surprised.

title: A hard truth from a mentor
settingKo: 승진에서 계속 밀리는 이유를 멘토가 솔직하게 말해 줍니다.

lines.text: Do you want the comfortable version or the useful version?
lines.ko: 편한 버전으로 들을래요, 쓸모 있는 버전으로 들을래요?

lines.text: The useful one, please. I've had enough of being told I'm almost ready.
lines.ko: 쓸모 있는 거요. 거의 준비됐다는 말은 이제 질렸어요.

lines.text: You're brilliant in the details, but leadership hasn't once heard you talk about where the business should go.
lines.ko: 디테일에선 탁월하지만 경영진은 당신이 사업의 방향을 말하는 걸 한 번도 못 들었어요.

lines.text: People get promoted for the problems they're seen to own, not just the tasks they finish.
lines.ko: 사람은 끝낸 업무가 아니라 책임지는 것으로 보이는 문제로 승진해요.

phrases.en: The comfortable version or the useful version?
The problems they're seen to own.

response.situationKo: 아끼는 후배에게 쓴소리를 해야 합니다. 상처 주지 않으면서 핵심을 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: Be honest with me. Why didn't I get the lead role?

answers.text: I'll be straight with you, because I think you can handle it. Your work is excellent, but you avoid conflict, and leads can't.
answers.noteKo: I'll be straight with you는 '솔직히 말할게'예요.

answers.text: What's missing isn't skill, it's visibility. People don't know what you're capable of.
If I were you, I'd volunteer for the messiest project next quarter and run it out loud.
answers.noteKo: run it out loud는 공개적으로 이끌라는 뜻이에요.

answers.text: Honestly? The gap is small. You just need to stop waiting for permission.
answers.noteKo: stop waiting for permission은 허락을 기다리지 말라는 거예요.

title: Small talk at a gala
settingKo: 자선 갈라 행사에서 모르는 사람과 품위 있게 대화합니다.

lines.text: I don't believe we've been introduced. Are you here with the foundation, or on the brave side of the auction?
lines.ko: 인사를 못 나눈 것 같네요. 재단 쪽이세요, 아니면 경매에서 용감하게 입찰하는 쪽이세요?

lines.text: Somewhere in between, I'm afraid. My firm sponsors a table, and I've been warned not to raise my hand by accident.
lines.ko: 그 중간쯤이에요. 회사가 테이블을 후원하는데 실수로 손 들지 말라는 경고를 받았어요.

lines.text: Wise advice. Last year someone waved at a friend and went home with a weekend in Tuscany.
lines.ko: 현명한 조언이네요. 작년에 누가 친구한테 손 흔들었다가 토스카나 주말 여행권을 낙찰받았거든요.

lines.text: There are worse fates. Still, I'll keep my hands firmly on my champagne.
lines.ko: 더 나쁜 운명도 있죠. 그래도 손은 샴페인 잔에 꼭 붙여 둘게요.

phrases.en: I don't believe we've been introduced.
There are worse fates.

response.situationKo: 격식 있는 자리에서 처음 만난 사람에게 재치 있게 말을 걸어 보세요.
response.prompt: Lovely evening, isn't it?

answers.text: It is. I must say, the string quartet is doing heroic work over all this chatter.
answers.noteKo: I must say는 격식 있는 감탄이에요.

answers.text: Rather. How do you know the hosts? I'm here through work, so I'm trying to look like I belong.
I was just thinking the same. Though I suspect the dessert table is the real star.
Beautiful. Have you been to one of these before, or is this your first?

title: Something doesn't add up
settingKo: 동료가 수치를 조작한 정황을 발견하고 믿을 만한 선배와 상의합니다.

lines.text: I think the trial results in the report were adjusted. The raw data simply doesn't support the conclusion.
lines.ko: 보고서의 시험 결과가 수정된 것 같아요. 원자료로는 그 결론이 나오지 않아요.

lines.text: That's serious. Before anything else, are you sure it isn't a legitimate correction you haven't seen documented?
lines.ko: 심각하네요. 무엇보다 먼저, 기록을 못 본 정당한 수정일 가능성은 없어요?

lines.text: I've checked twice. There's no note, and only one person had access to that file.
lines.ko: 두 번 확인했어요. 아무 기록도 없고 그 파일에 접근할 수 있는 사람은 한 명뿐이었어요.

lines.text: Then document everything, don't confront him yourself, and take it to the compliance team through the official channel.
lines.ko: 그럼 모든 걸 기록하고, 직접 따지지 말고, 공식 경로로 준법감시팀에 가져가요.

phrases.en: The data doesn't support the conclusion.
Through the official channel.

response.situationKo: 동료가 윤리적으로 애매한 부탁을 합니다. 단호하지만 관계를 지키며 거절해 보세요.
response.prompt: Could you just tweak the numbers a little so the quarter looks better? Everyone does it.

answers.text: I'm not comfortable doing that. What I can do is help you explain why the quarter was weak.
Honestly, I can't. If it ever came out, it would hurt both of us far more than a bad quarter.
I hear the pressure you're under, but that's a line I won't cross.
answers.noteKo: a line I won't cross는 넘지 않을 선이에요.

answers.text: Ha, no chance. Let's find a better story to tell with the real numbers.

title: When words aren't enough
settingKo: 아버지를 잃은 친구와 오랜만에 이야기를 나눕니다.

lines.text: Everyone keeps saying he's in a better place, and I know they mean well, but it makes me want to scream.
lines.ko: 다들 더 좋은 곳에 가셨다고 하는데, 좋은 뜻인 건 알지만 소리 지르고 싶어져.

lines.text: That makes complete sense. You don't need him to be in a better place; you need him here.
lines.ko: 완전히 이해돼. 아버지가 더 좋은 곳에 계실 필요는 없잖아. 여기 계셨으면 하는 거지.

lines.text: Exactly. Thank you for not trying to fix it.
lines.ko: 바로 그거야. 고치려고 하지 않아 줘서 고마워.

lines.text: I'm not going anywhere. Tell me about him, if you feel like it. What was he like on a Sunday?
lines.ko: 나 어디 안 가. 괜찮으면 아버지 얘기 해 줘. 일요일엔 어떤 분이셨어?

phrases.en: I know they mean well.
Thank you for not trying to fix it.

response.situationKo: 힘든 일을 겪은 친구가 아무 말도 하기 싫다고 합니다. 곁에 있어 주는 말을 해 보세요.
response.prompt: I don't really want to talk about it.

answers.text: That's completely okay. We don't have to talk. I'm happy just sitting here with you.
No pressure at all. Whenever you do, or don't, I'm here.
Fair enough. Want to watch something terrible and eat too much pizza instead?
Okay. I'll just drop off some food tomorrow, and you can ignore my texts guilt-free.

title: You had to be there
settingKo: 새로 온 동료에게 팀의 오래된 농담을 설명해 줍니다.

lines.text: Why does everyone say 'not the fish again' whenever someone suggests a team lunch?
lines.ko: 누가 팀 점심 얘기만 하면 왜 다들 '또 생선은 안 돼'라고 해요?

lines.text: Ah, you had to be there. Three years ago our old boss booked a seafood place for the whole team.
lines.ko: 아, 그 자리에 있었어야 해요. 3년 전 예전 팀장님이 팀 전체를 해산물 식당에 예약했거든요.

lines.text: Half of us were allergic, and he spent the entire lunch insisting the fish was basically vegetables.
lines.ko: 절반이 알레르기가 있었는데 그분은 점심 내내 생선은 거의 채소라고 우겼어요.

lines.text: That's incredible. I feel like I've just been initiated into a secret society.
lines.ko: 대박이네요. 비밀 결사에 막 입단한 기분이에요.

phrases.en: You had to be there.
I've been initiated into a secret society.

response.situationKo: 새 친구가 당신 무리의 농담을 이해 못 합니다. 웃기게 설명해 보세요.
response.prompt: Wait, why do you all call Dave 'the Captain'?

answers.text: Long story short: he once tried to sail a rental boat and ended up in the wrong country.
Basically, ever since that camping trip, he's insisted on leading us everywhere, and we're always lost.
Honestly, you had to be there. But it involves a canoe, a goose, and zero survival skills.
answers.noteKo: 세 가지 요소 나열로 웃음을 줘요.

answers.text: Short version: confidence with no sense of direction. We'll tell you the full saga over drinks.

title: Is hustle culture over?
settingKo: 팟캐스트 진행자 두 명이 '갈아 넣는' 업무 문화에 대해 토론합니다.

lines.text: The idea that you need to sacrifice your twenties to make it feels increasingly outdated.
lines.ko: 성공하려면 20대를 희생해야 한다는 생각은 점점 구식으로 느껴져요.

lines.text: I'd push back slightly. Some things genuinely reward obsession, and pretending otherwise is a bit dishonest.
lines.ko: 살짝 반박할게요. 어떤 일은 정말로 집착에 보상하고, 그렇지 않은 척하는 건 좀 정직하지 않아요.

lines.text: Sure, but there's a difference between choosing intensity and having it demanded of you by an employer.
lines.ko: 그렇죠, 근데 강도를 스스로 선택하는 것과 고용주가 요구하는 건 달라요.

lines.text: That's the real distinction, isn't it? Ambition is fine; unpaid ambition on someone else's behalf is the problem.
lines.ko: 그게 진짜 구분이죠. 야망은 괜찮아요. 남을 위한 무급 야망이 문제죠.

options: 스스로 선택한 강도와 강요된 강도는 다르다

phrases.en: I'd push back slightly.
That's the real distinction, isn't it?

response.situationKo: 일과 삶의 균형에 대한 자신의 철학을 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: Do you think working long hours is necessary to succeed?

answers.text: In some seasons, yes, but not as a permanent lifestyle. The danger is when the season never ends.
I'd say focus matters more than hours. Six sharp hours beat twelve distracted ones.
It depends on whether you're building something you own. Grinding for someone else's dream is different.
Honestly, burnout set me back more than any slow year ever did.

title: The best of times, the worst of times
settingKo: 디킨스의 '두 도시 이야기' 첫 문장을 요즘 상황에 빗대어 이야기합니다.

lines.text: It was the best of times, it was the worst of times. Dickens could have been describing our startup this year.
lines.ko: 최고의 시절이자 최악의 시절이었다. 디킨스가 올해 우리 스타트업을 묘사한 것 같아.

lines.text: Record sales and half the team quitting. That's about as Dickensian as it gets.
lines.ko: 기록적인 매출에 팀 절반 퇴사. 그보다 더 디킨스스러울 수 없지.

lines.text: What I love about that opening is that it refuses to choose. Both things are true at once.
lines.ko: 그 첫 문장이 좋은 건 어느 한쪽을 고르지 않는다는 거야. 둘 다 동시에 사실이야.

lines.text: Maybe that's the lesson for us too: celebrate the wins without pretending the losses aren't real.
lines.ko: 우리한테 주는 교훈도 그걸지 몰라. 손실이 없는 척하지 않으면서 성과를 축하하는 것.

phrases.en: It was the best of times, it was the worst of times.
Both things are true at once.

response.situationKo: 올해를 한 문장으로 요약해 보세요. 명언이나 비유를 섞어도 좋아요.
response.prompt: If you had to sum up your year in one line, what would it be?

answers.text: A year of quiet progress: nothing dramatic, but I'm stronger than I was in January.
answers.noteKo: A year of ~로 한 해를 규정해요.

answers.text: Honestly, the best of times and the worst of times, just like Dickens said.
Like a rollercoaster I didn't remember buying a ticket for.
If I'm honest, it was the year I finally stopped apologizing for wanting more.

title: Fighting for your team
settingKo: 인사 위원회에서 팀원의 승진을 강하게 지지합니다.

lines.text: She's only been with us eighteen months. Isn't it a bit premature to put her up for senior?
lines.ko: 입사한 지 18개월밖에 안 됐어요. 시니어로 올리기엔 좀 이르지 않나요?

lines.text: If we measured tenure, perhaps. But she's already doing the job, and has been for six months.
lines.ko: 근속으로 따지면 그럴지도요. 하지만 이미 그 일을 하고 있고 6개월째예요.

lines.text: She led the migration that everyone else had quietly avoided, and it landed on time and under budget.
lines.ko: 다들 슬쩍 피하던 이전 작업을 이끌었고, 일정 안에 예산보다 적게 끝냈어요.

lines.text: That's compelling. If we don't recognize it, I suspect someone else will, and she'll walk.
lines.ko: 설득력 있네요. 우리가 인정하지 않으면 다른 누군가가 알아보고 그녀는 떠나겠죠.

phrases.en: She's already doing the job.
Someone else will, and she'll walk.
phrases.ko: 다른 누군가가 알아보고 그녀는 떠날 거예요.

response.situationKo: 회의에서 팀원의 공로가 다른 사람에게 돌아갔습니다. 정중하게 바로잡아 보세요.
response.prompt: Great work on the launch, Mark. Really impressive.

answers.text: I'd like to add that Priya designed the entire rollout plan. Credit where it's due.
answers.noteKo: Credit where it's due는 공을 제대로 돌리자는 말이에요.

answers.text: It's worth mentioning that the hard part was Priya's work behind the scenes.
answers.noteKo: behind the scenes는 보이지 않는 곳에서예요.

answers.text: Absolutely, and a huge shout-out to Priya, who actually cracked the data problem.
Thanks on behalf of the team. Priya deserves most of it, honestly.

title: Defending a thesis
settingKo: 박사 논문 구술 심사에서 심사위원의 날카로운 질문에 답합니다.

lines.text: Your argument rests heavily on interviews from a single city. How confident are you that it generalizes?
lines.ko: 당신 주장은 한 도시의 인터뷰에 크게 기대고 있어요. 일반화할 수 있다고 얼마나 확신하나요?

lines.text: Not entirely, and I say as much in chapter six. I'd frame it as a theory to be tested rather than a universal claim.
lines.ko: 완전히는 아니고, 6장에서도 그렇게 썼습니다. 보편적 주장이라기보다 검증할 이론으로 봐 주셨으면 해요.

lines.text: Then what would falsify it?
lines.ko: 그럼 무엇이 그 이론을 반증할까요?

lines.text: If cities with similar housing pressure showed no rise in informal subletting, my mechanism would be in serious trouble.
lines.ko: 비슷한 주거 압박을 받는 도시에서 비공식 전대가 늘지 않는다면 제 메커니즘은 심각한 문제에 빠지겠죠.

phrases.en: I say as much in chapter six.
What would falsify it?

response.situationKo: 전문가가 당신 의견의 약점을 지적합니다. 인정하면서도 논지를 지켜 보세요.
response.prompt: Isn't your whole argument based on a single example?

answers.text: It's true that the example is singular. However, the pattern it reveals has been documented elsewhere.
I'd concede the evidence is thin. Nonetheless, the broader point still holds.
Fair challenge. What I'd argue is that the example is illustrative, not proof.
Guilty as charged on that one, but the logic doesn't depend on it.
answers.noteKo: Guilty as charged는 '인정합니다'의 재치 있는 표현이에요.

title: I've forgotten your name
settingKo: 아는 사람인데 이름이 생각나지 않아 재치 있게 넘깁니다.

lines.text: Hello again! Lovely to see you. How did the move to Lisbon go?
lines.ko: 또 뵙네요! 반가워요. 리스본 이사는 어떻게 됐어요?

lines.text: Wonderfully, thanks. And I'm mortified, because your face is so familiar but your name has completely escaped me.
lines.ko: 아주 잘 됐어요, 고마워요. 그런데 너무 민망하네요. 얼굴은 정말 익숙한데 이름이 완전히 생각이 안 나요.

lines.text: Don't worry at all, it happens to everyone. It's Clara, from the design conference last spring.
lines.ko: 전혀 걱정 마세요, 다들 그래요. 지난봄 디자인 콘퍼런스의 클라라예요.

lines.text: Clara, of course! You gave that brilliant talk on accessibility.
lines.ko: 클라라, 맞다! 접근성에 대해 멋진 발표를 하셨죠.

options: 솔직하게 이름이 기억 안 난다고 했다

phrases.en: Your name has completely escaped me.
It happens to everyone.

response.situationKo: 모임에서 상대가 내 이름을 잘못 불렀습니다. 어색하지 않게 바로잡아 보세요.
response.prompt: Great to see you again, Michelle!

answers.text: So close! It's actually Michaela, but people mix them up all the time.
Lovely to see you too. It's Michaela, actually, but honestly, an easy mistake.
No worries at all, it's Michaela. I'm terrible with names myself.
answers.noteKo: 자기도 그렇다고 하면 상대가 덜 민망해요.

answers.text: Ha, Michelle's my evil twin. I'm Michaela.

title: Should we know everything?
settingKo: 유전자 검사 결과를 알고 싶은지에 대해 친구와 깊이 이야기합니다.

lines.text: The test can tell me if I carry the gene for the disease my grandmother had. I'm not sure I want to know.
lines.ko: 검사하면 할머니가 앓던 병의 유전자가 있는지 알 수 있대. 알고 싶은지 모르겠어.

lines.text: That's such a personal call. Would knowing change anything you'd actually do?
lines.ko: 정말 개인적인 결정이네. 안다고 실제로 네가 할 일이 달라질까?

lines.text: Possibly. There's no cure, but early screening could buy years, and it might affect whether we have children.
lines.ko: 아마도. 치료법은 없지만 조기 검진으로 몇 년을 벌 수 있고, 아이를 가질지에도 영향을 줄 수 있어.

lines.text: Then maybe talk to a genetic counselor first. They're trained to help people weigh exactly this.
lines.ko: 그럼 먼저 유전 상담사와 얘기해 봐. 바로 이런 걸 따져 보도록 훈련받은 사람들이야.

phrases.en: That's such a personal call.
It could buy years.

response.situationKo: 정답이 없는 윤리적 질문에 대해 신중하게 의견을 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: Would you want to know the exact date you'll die, if you could?

answers.text: Part of me would, to plan properly, but I think it would quietly poison every ordinary day.
Probably not. I'd rather live as if there's time, and occasionally be surprised.
Honestly, yes. I'm a planner. On the other hand, I'd probably count down obsessively.
I don't think anyone could handle that knowledge gracefully, however rational they claim to be.

title: Unconscious bias
settingKo: 채용 회의에서 동료의 무의식적 편견을 부드럽게 짚습니다.

lines.text: I'd go with James. He just feels like a better culture fit, you know?
lines.ko: 제임스로 가죠. 그냥 문화적으로 더 잘 맞는 느낌이잖아요.

lines.text: Can I gently push on that? When we say culture fit, sometimes we mean someone who reminds us of ourselves.
lines.ko: 그 부분을 살짝 짚어도 될까요? 문화 적합성이라고 할 때 때로는 우리와 닮은 사람을 뜻하기도 해요.

lines.text: On the actual scorecard, Amina outscored him on every technical question.
lines.ko: 실제 평가표에선 아미나가 모든 기술 질문에서 그보다 높은 점수를 받았어요.

lines.text: Hm. That's fair. Let's go back to the criteria and decide on those, not on gut feeling.
lines.ko: 음. 맞는 말이에요. 평가 기준으로 돌아가서 직감 말고 그걸로 정하죠.

options: 문화 적합성이 편견일 수 있다는 점

phrases.en: Can I gently push on that?
Not on gut feeling.

response.situationKo: 동료가 은근히 편견 섞인 농담을 합니다. 분위기를 깨지 않으면서 선을 그어 보세요.
response.prompt: Ha, typical engineers, no social skills at all, right?

answers.text: To be fair, some of the best communicators I know are engineers.
I'm not sure that's fair. In my experience, it varies a lot.
Ha, I'd push back on that one. Our team would roast you for saying it.
That's a bit of a stereotype, isn't it? Let's not lump everyone together.

title: Objecting to the plan
settingKo: 주민 공청회에서 동네 개발 계획에 대해 논리적으로 이의를 제기합니다.

lines.text: I'm not opposed to new housing in principle. We desperately need it.
lines.ko: 원칙적으로 새 주택에 반대하지 않아요. 절실히 필요하죠.

lines.text: My concern is that this plan adds four hundred homes and not a single school place or doctor's surgery.
lines.ko: 제 우려는 이 계획이 주택 400호를 늘리면서 학교 정원이나 병원은 하나도 늘리지 않는다는 거예요.

lines.text: The developer has committed to a contribution for local services.
lines.ko: 개발사는 지역 서비스에 기여금을 내기로 약속했습니다.

lines.text: A contribution isn't a building. I'd ask the council to make planning permission conditional on the school being delivered first.
lines.ko: 기여금은 건물이 아니에요. 학교가 먼저 지어지는 것을 조건으로 허가를 내 달라고 시의회에 요청합니다.

options: 학교를 먼저 짓는 것을 허가 조건으로

phrases.en: I'm not opposed in principle.
A contribution isn't a building.

response.situationKo: 공적인 자리에서 정책에 대해 짧고 설득력 있게 의견을 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: We'll take one more comment from the floor.

answers.text: Thank you. My name is Min, and I'd like to raise one specific point about parking.
I'd urge the council to publish the traffic study before any vote takes place.
Speaking as a parent, the crossing outside the school simply isn't safe at peak times.
Quick one: residents were given two weeks' notice. That's not real consultation.

title: Football banter
settingKo: 라이벌 팀 팬인 동료와 월요일 아침에 농담을 주고받습니다.

lines.text: Morning! Rough weekend? I hear your lot managed to lose to a team that was bottom of the league.
lines.ko: 좋은 아침! 주말 힘들었지? 너네 팀이 리그 꼴찌한테 졌다며.

lines.text: Bold words from someone whose team hasn't won away from home since before smartphones were invented.
lines.ko: 스마트폰이 발명되기 전 이후로 원정에서 이겨 본 적 없는 팀 팬치고는 말이 세네.

lines.text: Ouch. Fair, but at least we're consistent. Consistently disappointing, admittedly.
lines.ko: 아야. 맞아, 그래도 우린 한결같잖아. 한결같이 실망스럽긴 하지만.

lines.text: Loser buys coffee after Saturday's derby?
lines.ko: 토요일 더비 지는 쪽이 커피 사기?

options: 더비에서 지는 팀 팬이 커피를 산다

phrases.en: Bold words from someone whose team...
Loser buys coffee.

response.situationKo: 친구가 당신 응원 팀이 졌다고 놀립니다. 재치 있게 받아쳐 보세요.
response.prompt: Ha! Three-nil! Did you even watch the second half?

answers.text: Says the person whose team needed a penalty to beat a bunch of part-timers.
answers.noteKo: Says the person ~은 '~한 사람이 할 말은 아니지'예요.

answers.text: We'll see who's laughing in May. It's a marathon, not a sprint.
answers.noteKo: a marathon, not a sprint는 길게 봐야 한다는 말이에요.

answers.text: Remind me, when did your lot last win a trophy? I'll wait.
At least we play attractive football. Results are overrated.

title: To be, or not to be
settingKo: 큰 결정을 몇 달째 못 내리는 친구에게 햄릿을 빗대어 말합니다.

lines.text: Move to Berlin or stay? I've been going back and forth for three months, and I'm exhausting myself.
lines.ko: 베를린으로 갈까 남을까? 석 달째 오락가락하느라 지쳤어.

lines.text: To be, or not to be. You're turning into Hamlet, minus the castle and the ghost.
lines.ko: 사느냐 죽느냐. 성이랑 유령만 빼면 너 햄릿이 돼 가고 있어.

lines.text: Remember how his overthinking worked out? Not brilliantly. Sometimes the worst choice is no choice.
lines.ko: 그 사람 생각 과잉의 결말 기억나? 좋지 않았지. 때로는 결정을 안 하는 게 최악의 선택이야.

lines.text: Fair. I'll give myself until Friday, and then I'm booking a flight or unpacking for good.
lines.ko: 맞네. 금요일까지 시간을 줄게. 그다음엔 비행기를 예약하든 짐을 영원히 풀든 할 거야.

options: 결정을 안 하는 게 최악일 수 있다

phrases.en: To be, or not to be.
Sometimes the worst choice is no choice.
phrases.ko: 때로는 결정을 안 하는 게 최악의 선택이야.

response.situationKo: 친구가 결정을 못 내립니다. 결정하도록 등을 떠밀어 보세요.
response.prompt: I just can't decide, and it's driving me mad.

answers.text: Flip a coin. Not to decide, but to notice which side you're secretly hoping for.
Set a deadline and write down what would make each option a mistake.
Imagine yourself ten years from now. Which version of you would you rather explain this to?
If you had to answer in three seconds? Go. That's your gut.

title: An investment in knowledge
settingKo: 회사 교육비 삭감을 두고 프랭클린의 말을 인용해 반대합니다.

lines.text: Training is the easiest line to cut. Nobody notices it's gone until a year later.
lines.ko: 교육비가 가장 쉽게 깎이는 항목이죠. 1년이 지나야 없어진 걸 알아채니까요.

lines.text: Which is precisely the problem. Benjamin Franklin said an investment in knowledge pays the best interest.
lines.ko: 바로 그게 문제예요. 벤저민 프랭클린은 지식에 대한 투자가 최고의 이자를 낳는다고 했죠.

lines.text: If we cut it now, we'll pay recruiters twice as much next year to hire the skills we refused to grow.
lines.ko: 지금 깎으면 내년에 우리가 키우기를 거부한 역량을 채용하느라 헤드헌터에게 두 배를 낼 거예요.

lines.text: A persuasive point, and a cheaper one than I'd like to admit.
lines.ko: 설득력 있네요. 인정하기 싫을 만큼 돈이 덜 드는 논리이기도 하고요.

phrases.en: An investment in knowledge pays the best interest.
phrases.ko: 지식에 대한 투자가 최고의 이자를 낳는다. (프랭클린)

phrases.en: Precisely the problem.

response.situationKo: 자신을 위한 공부나 경험에 돈을 쓰는 이유를 명언을 섞어 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: Why spend so much on courses? Isn't that money better saved?

answers.text: As Franklin said, an investment in knowledge pays the best interest. It compounds like nothing else.
I see it as investing in the one asset nobody can take from me.
Savings sit still. Skills keep paying, in the long run anyway.
Honestly? The course paid for itself with my first raise.
answers.noteKo: paid for itself는 본전을 뽑았다는 뜻이에요.

title: Feedback for the CEO
settingKo: 대표가 솔직한 피드백을 요청하자 조심스럽지만 분명하게 말합니다.

lines.text: You've worked with me for two years. What's one thing I do that makes your job harder?
lines.ko: 2년간 나랑 일했잖아요. 내가 하는 일 중 당신 일을 더 어렵게 만드는 게 하나 있다면?

lines.text: Since you asked, and I mean this respectfully: decisions you make in hallway conversations often reverse what the team agreed in meetings.
lines.ko: 물으셨으니, 존중하는 마음으로 말씀드리면, 복도에서 내리시는 결정이 회의에서 팀이 합의한 걸 자주 뒤집어요.

lines.text: Ouch. I genuinely didn't realize I was doing that.
lines.ko: 아프네요. 정말 내가 그러는 줄 몰랐어요.

lines.text: Most people wouldn't. A simple fix might be sending a one-line note whenever you change course, so we're not blindsided.
lines.ko: 대부분 모를 거예요. 방향을 바꾸실 때마다 한 줄 메모만 보내 주셔도 저희가 허를 찔리지 않을 거예요.

options: 방향을 바꿀 때 한 줄 메모를 보낸다

phrases.en: Since you asked, and I mean this respectfully...
So we're not blindsided.

response.situationKo: 상사가 솔직한 의견을 원한다고 합니다. 예의 바르지만 분명하게 문제를 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: Be brutally honest. What should I stop doing?

answers.text: Since you asked: when you reply to emails at midnight, the team feels they have to as well.
Respectfully, one thing would be letting people finish presenting before you jump in with solutions.
It would help if priorities changed less often. The impact is a lot of half-finished work.
Brutally? Fewer surprise Friday deadlines. Our weekends would thank you.

title: Repairing a friendship
settingKo: 뒷말 때문에 멀어진 친구에게 진심으로 사과합니다.

lines.text: I owe you an apology, and I don't want to dress it up. I repeated something you told me in confidence, and that was wrong.
lines.ko: 사과할 게 있어. 포장하지 않을게. 네가 비밀로 말한 걸 내가 옮겼고, 그건 잘못이었어.

lines.text: It wasn't just that you said it. It was finding out from someone else.
lines.ko: 네가 말한 것만이 아니라, 다른 사람한테서 알게 된 게 더 컸어.

lines.text: I know. I've no excuse, only an explanation, and I'm not going to hide behind it.
lines.ko: 알아. 변명은 없고 설명만 있는데, 그 뒤에 숨진 않을게.

lines.text: I appreciate you not making excuses. It'll take a while, but I'd rather work on this than lose you.
lines.ko: 변명하지 않아서 고마워. 시간은 좀 걸리겠지만 널 잃느니 이걸 풀어 가고 싶어.

phrases.en: I don't want to dress it up.
I've no excuse, only an explanation.

response.situationKo: 친구에게 큰 실수를 했습니다. 변명 없이 진심으로 사과해 보세요.
response.prompt: Why did you do it?

answers.text: There's no excuse. I was careless with something that mattered to you, and I'm truly sorry.
I was wrong, full stop. I understand if you need time, and I'll wait.
Honestly, I wasn't thinking. I'd like to make it right, however long that takes.
I messed up. I know trust doesn't come back overnight, but I'm not going anywhere.

title: Telling investors bad news
settingKo: 스타트업 대표가 기존 투자자에게 낮은 가치로 투자를 받아야 한다고 알립니다.

lines.text: I'll get straight to it. We have about five months of runway, and the only term sheet on the table values us lower than last round.
lines.ko: 바로 말씀드릴게요. 운영 자금이 5개월 정도 남았고, 지금 유일한 투자 조건은 지난 라운드보다 가치를 낮게 매겨요.

lines.text: That's disappointing. Why didn't we see this coming earlier?
lines.ko: 실망스럽네요. 왜 더 일찍 예상하지 못했죠?

lines.text: Partly my fault. I was too optimistic about the enterprise pipeline, and two big deals slipped into next year.
lines.ko: 일부는 제 탓이에요. 기업 영업 전망을 너무 낙관했고 큰 거래 두 건이 내년으로 밀렸어요.

lines.text: Taking the round keeps us alive long enough for those deals to close, which is where the real value is.
lines.ko: 이 투자를 받으면 그 거래들이 성사될 때까지 버틸 수 있고, 진짜 가치는 거기에 있어요.

phrases.en: I'll get straight to it.
Two big deals slipped into next year.
phrases.ko: 큰 거래 두 건이 내년으로 밀렸어요.

response.situationKo: 이해관계자에게 계획이 틀어졌다는 소식을 전해야 합니다. 책임감 있게 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: So how did we end up here?

answers.text: I'll be candid: in hindsight, I underestimated how long hiring would take, and I own that.
Partly my fault, partly the market. What matters now is the plan, and here it is.
What we've learned is that our forecasts were too rosy. The plan now uses conservative numbers only.
Short answer: we bet on the wrong channel. Long answer's in the deck, but I'm not hiding from it.

title: We don't know yet
settingKo: 검사 결과가 애매하다는 말을 듣고 의사와 차분히 이야기합니다.

lines.text: I'll be honest with you: the scan shows something, but it's genuinely ambiguous. It could well be nothing.
lines.ko: 솔직히 말씀드리면 영상에 뭔가 보이는데 정말 애매해요. 아무것도 아닐 가능성도 충분해요.

lines.text: I appreciate the honesty. What are the realistic possibilities, from most to least likely?
lines.ko: 솔직하게 말해 주셔서 감사해요. 현실적인 가능성을 가장 높은 것부터 알려 주시겠어요?

lines.text: Most likely a harmless cyst. Less likely, something we'd want to treat early. A biopsy would settle it.
lines.ko: 가장 가능성 높은 건 무해한 낭종이에요. 가능성은 낮지만 일찍 치료해야 할 무언가일 수도 있고요. 조직 검사로 확실해질 거예요.

lines.text: Then I'd rather know than wonder. How soon can we schedule it?
lines.ko: 그럼 궁금해하느니 알고 싶어요. 얼마나 빨리 잡을 수 있나요?

phrases.en: It's genuinely ambiguous.
I'd rather know than wonder.

response.situationKo: 전문가가 애매한 답만 합니다. 핵심을 정확히 물어보세요.
response.prompt: It's hard to say at this stage.

answers.text: I understand. If you had to guess, which way would you lean?
answers.noteKo: If you had to guess로 의견을 끌어내요.

answers.text: What would change your answer? What are we waiting to find out?
Realistically, what's the worst case, and how likely is it?
Fair enough. So what's the next step, and when?

title: Ask not
settingKo: 봉사 모임에서 케네디의 유명한 연설 구절로 이야기를 나눕니다.

lines.text: Ask not what your country can do for you; ask what you can do for your country. People still quote it sixty years on.
lines.ko: 국가가 당신을 위해 무엇을 할지 묻지 말고, 당신이 국가를 위해 무엇을 할지 물으라. 60년이 지나도 인용되죠.

lines.text: The structure is what makes it stick. He flips the same words around, so you can't help but remember it.
lines.ko: 구조 때문에 기억에 남아요. 같은 단어를 뒤집어 놓으니 기억하지 않을 수 없죠.

lines.text: Some people find it a bit one-sided, as if citizens owe everything and the state owes nothing.
lines.ko: 어떤 사람들은 시민은 모든 걸 빚지고 국가는 아무것도 빚지지 않는 것처럼 좀 일방적이라고 봐요.

lines.text: Maybe, but in a room full of volunteers on a Saturday morning, it lands rather well.
lines.ko: 그럴지도요. 그래도 토요일 아침 자원봉사자로 가득한 방에서는 꽤 와닿네요.

phrases.en: Ask not what your country can do for you.
phrases.ko: 국가가 당신을 위해 무엇을 할지 묻지 말라. (케네디, 1961)

phrases.en: You can't help but remember it.

response.situationKo: 같은 단어를 뒤집는 표현(대구법)으로 짧은 다짐을 만들어 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: Give us a motto for the new year, Kennedy-style.

answers.text: Don't wait for the right moment; make the moment right.
Less scrolling, more strolling.
Rather than asking what the team can give me, I'll ask what I can give the team.
Work to live, not live to work.

title: Looking at the stars
settingKo: 힘든 시기의 친구에게 오스카 와일드의 문장을 건넵니다.

lines.text: I've been rejected by eleven publishers. At this point I'm wondering why I bother.
lines.ko: 출판사 열한 곳에서 거절당했어. 이쯤 되니 내가 왜 이러나 싶어.

lines.text: Oscar Wilde wrote that we are all in the gutter, but some of us are looking at the stars.
lines.ko: 오스카 와일드가 썼잖아. 우리는 모두 시궁창에 있지만 그중 몇은 별을 보고 있다고.

lines.text: Eleven rejections means you finished a book and sent it out eleven times. Most people never get to the gutter, let alone the stars.
lines.ko: 거절 열한 번은 책을 끝내고 열한 번 내보냈다는 뜻이야. 대부분은 시궁창에도 못 가, 별은 말할 것도 없고.

lines.text: That's an annoyingly good way of putting it. Fine, number twelve goes out tomorrow.
lines.ko: 짜증 나게 좋은 표현이네. 좋아, 열두 번째는 내일 보낸다.

phrases.en: We are all in the gutter, but some of us are looking at the stars.
phrases.ko: 우리는 모두 시궁창에 있지만 그중 몇은 별을 보고 있다. (오스카 와일드)

phrases.en: Let alone...

response.situationKo: 실패로 낙담한 친구를 시각을 바꿔 주는 말로 격려해 보세요.
response.prompt: I failed the exam again. Maybe I'm just not cut out for this.
keywords: another way to look at it

answers.text: Another way to look at it: every attempt shows you exactly where the gaps are. You're closer than last time.
answers.noteKo: Another way to look at it으로 관점을 바꿔요.

answers.text: Failing twice means you tried twice. Most people quit after once.
Not cut out for it? You're the most stubborn person I know. That's exactly what this takes.
I'd gently suggest that persistence is the skill being tested here, and you have plenty of it.

title: A truth universally acknowledged
settingKo: 결혼을 재촉하는 부모님 이야기를 제인 오스틴의 문장에 빗대어 웃으며 나눕니다.

lines.text: My mother has set me up with her friend's son again. Third time this year.
lines.ko: 엄마가 또 친구 아들이랑 소개팅을 잡았어. 올해만 세 번째야.

lines.text: It is a truth universally acknowledged that a single woman in possession of a good job must be in want of a husband.
lines.ko: 좋은 직장을 가진 미혼 여성은 남편을 원하는 게 틀림없다는 건 누구나 인정하는 진리이지.

lines.text: Ha! Austen wrote it about a rich single man, but my mother has clearly adapted it for the modern market.
lines.ko: 하! 오스틴은 부유한 미혼 남자에 대해 쓴 건데, 우리 엄마는 확실히 현대 시장에 맞게 각색했네.

lines.text: Two hundred years later, and the mothers haven't changed a bit.
lines.ko: 200년이 지났는데 엄마들은 하나도 안 변했어.

gist.questionKo: 원래 오스틴의 문장은 누구에 대한 것인가요?

phrases.en: It is a truth universally acknowledged...
They haven't changed a bit.

response.situationKo: 가족의 잔소리를 재치 있게 받아넘기는 말을 해 보세요.
response.prompt: So when are you going to settle down?

answers.text: The moment I find someone who's as patient as you are, Mum. You'll be the first to know.
In my own time, I promise. I'm actually quite happy right now.
As soon as the housing market settles down, presumably.
I'll let you know, but I'd love it if we could talk about something else tonight.

title: A pun-ishing conversation
settingKo: 말장난을 좋아하는 동료들과 커피 머신 앞에서 농담을 주고받습니다.

lines.text: The coffee machine's broken again. Honestly, it's grounds for dismissal.
lines.ko: 커피 머신 또 고장 났어. 솔직히 해고 사유야. (grounds: 사유/커피 찌꺼기)

lines.text: Don't be so bitter. It's clearly just going through a rough patch.
lines.ko: 너무 쓰게 굴지 마. 그냥 힘든 시기를 겪고 있는 거야.

lines.text: I'd fix it myself, but I don't have the right espresso-tise.
lines.ko: 내가 고치고 싶은데 맞는 에스프레소… 아니 전문성이 없어. (expertise 말장난)

lines.text: Okay, that one was terrible. I'm leaving before this brews into something worse.
lines.ko: 좋아, 그건 최악이었어. 더 나쁜 걸로 우러나기 전에 갈게.

phrases.en: It's grounds for dismissal.
It's going through a rough patch.

response.situationKo: 동료의 말장난에 같은 방식으로 맞받아쳐 보세요.
response.prompt: Why did the scarecrow win an award? Because he was outstanding in his field.

answers.text: That's so corny. Which, to be fair, is very on-brand for a scarecrow.
answers.noteKo: corny는 진부한, 옥수수 같은이라는 이중 의미예요.

answers.text: Groan. I'll see your scarecrow and raise you a cow who became an astronaut. He went to the moooon.
answers.noteKo: I'll see your ~ and raise you는 포커식 받아치기예요.

answers.text: Terrible. Absolutely terrible. Tell me another one.
I'm not even going to dignify that with a laugh. Okay, maybe a small one.

title: Sorry, say that again?
settingKo: 스코틀랜드 출신 동료의 빠른 억양을 잘 못 알아들어 정중하게 다시 묻습니다.

lines.text: Aye, it's dreich the day, so we'll no bother wi' the walk tae the loch.
lines.ko: 그래, 오늘 날씨가 우중충해서 호수까지 걷는 건 관두자. (스코틀랜드 방언)

lines.text: Sorry, I caught 'walk' and 'loch', but I'm afraid 'dreich' completely lost me.
lines.ko: 미안, '산책'이랑 '호수'는 알아들었는데 '드리크'에서 완전히 놓쳤어.

lines.text: Ha, sorry! Dreich means grey, wet, and miserable. Basically, today's weather is rubbish.
lines.ko: 하, 미안! 드리크는 흐리고 축축하고 우울하다는 뜻이야. 그냥 오늘 날씨가 별로라는 거지.

lines.text: Brilliant, I'm stealing that word. It describes most Mondays perfectly.
lines.ko: 멋지다, 그 단어 훔쳐 갈게. 대부분의 월요일을 완벽하게 표현하네.

phrases.en: That completely lost me.
I'm stealing that word.

response.situationKo: 상대의 말이 너무 빠르거나 억양이 강해서 놓쳤어요. 정중하게 다시 부탁해 보세요.
response.prompt: Ye ken whit ah mean? It wis pure mental!

answers.text: Sorry, I caught the end but missed the start. Could you say it one more time?
I'm afraid 'pure mental' lost me. Is that good or bad?
Ha, give me a second, my ears are still warming up. A bit slower?
Would you mind repeating that? I'm still tuning in to the accent, but I love it.

title: Cross-examination
settingKo: 모의 재판에서 증인의 진술 모순을 날카롭게 짚습니다.

lines.text: You told the police you were home all evening. Is that correct?
lines.ko: 경찰에 저녁 내내 집에 있었다고 진술했죠. 맞습니까?

lines.text: Yes, I watched television and went to bed around eleven.
lines.ko: 네, 텔레비전을 보다가 11시쯤 잤어요.

lines.text: Then perhaps you can explain why your phone connected to a mast across town at nine forty-five.
lines.ko: 그렇다면 9시 45분에 왜 당신 휴대폰이 도시 반대편 기지국에 연결됐는지 설명해 주시겠어요?

lines.text: I, well, I may have popped out briefly. I didn't think it was relevant.
lines.ko: 저, 그러니까, 잠깐 나갔을 수도 있어요. 관련 있다고 생각 안 했어요.

phrases.en: Perhaps you can explain why...
I didn't think it was relevant.

response.situationKo: 상대 주장의 모순을 정중하지만 날카롭게 지적해 보세요.
response.prompt: We've always been completely transparent with our customers.

answers.text: Then perhaps you can explain why the fee was only mentioned on page forty of the terms.
How do you reconcile that with the three hundred complaints about hidden charges?
With respect, earlier you said you'd never heard of the issue. Which is it?
answers.noteKo: Which is it?은 둘 중 무엇이냐고 몰아세워요.

answers.text: Completely? Even the email you sent at two a.m. changing the price?

title: Diplomatic language
settingKo: 국제 회의 후 기자회견에서 외교관이 신중하게 말을 고릅니다.

lines.text: Would you describe today's talks as a failure?
lines.ko: 오늘 회담을 실패라고 보십니까?

lines.text: I would describe them as frank and substantive. Both sides now understand each other's positions with considerable clarity.
lines.ko: 솔직하고 실질적이었다고 하겠습니다. 양측이 이제 서로의 입장을 상당히 분명하게 이해하게 됐죠.

lines.text: So no agreement, then?
lines.ko: 그러니까 합의는 없었다는 거죠?

lines.text: Not yet. But we've agreed to keep talking, which, given where we started, is not nothing.
lines.ko: 아직은요. 하지만 대화를 계속하기로 했고, 출발점을 생각하면 그건 결코 작은 일이 아닙니다.

options: 의견 차가 컸지만 대화는 이어 간다

phrases.en: Frank and substantive.
phrases.ko: 솔직하고 실질적인. (의견 차가 컸다는 외교적 표현)

phrases.en: Which is not nothing.

response.situationKo: 결과가 안 좋았던 프로젝트에 대해 외교적으로 표현해 보세요.
response.prompt: Be honest, was the pilot a disaster?

answers.text: I'd describe it as a valuable learning experience, with considerable room for improvement.
Let's say the results were mixed, and the lessons were very clear.
Not a success yet, but we now know exactly what not to do, which is progress of a kind.
Diplomatically? It was educational. Undiplomatically? Ouch.

title: I was wrong about that
settingKo: 지난 회의에서 했던 주장이 틀렸음을 알고 팀 앞에서 정정합니다.

lines.text: Before we start, I need to correct something. Last week I argued the drop in sign-ups was seasonal.
lines.ko: 시작하기 전에 정정할 게 있어요. 지난주 가입자 감소가 계절 탓이라고 주장했죠.

lines.text: Having dug into the data, I was wrong. It started the day we changed the sign-up form.
lines.ko: 데이터를 파 보니 제가 틀렸어요. 가입 양식을 바꾼 날부터 시작됐더라고요.

lines.text: Thanks for flagging that. It's not easy to walk something back in front of everyone.
lines.ko: 알려 줘서 고마워요. 모두 앞에서 말을 거둬들이는 게 쉽지 않잖아요.

lines.text: Better now than after we've spent a month fixing the wrong problem.
lines.ko: 엉뚱한 문제를 한 달 고친 뒤보다는 지금이 낫죠.

phrases.en: Having dug into the data, I was wrong.
It's not easy to walk something back.

response.situationKo: 이전에 확신했던 의견이 틀렸습니다. 팀 앞에서 깔끔하게 인정해 보세요.
response.prompt: Didn't you say last month that the new feature would definitely work?

answers.text: I did, and I was wrong. In light of the numbers, I'd now recommend we roll it back.
I stand corrected. What I've learned is that our users value speed over features.
Fair hit. I was overconfident, and the data says so pretty clearly.
I did say that. I'd rather change my mind than defend a bad call.
